// Package badpkg is a synthetic KNOWN-BAD fixture for
// collectionprefix_conformance_test.go's
// TestEveryStoreConstructionRoutesThroughSeam. TestBadPkgBypassesSeam
// constructs a store directly with a non-nil client, bypassing any seam
// entirely — the exact bypass the real gate exists to catch. This fixture
// must scan dirty with TWO findings, one per bypass shape:
//   1. a raw collection-name LITERAL passed inline;
//   2. the same raw name bound to a local VARIABLE first — invisible to
//      the original literal-only rule, and the reason that rule was
//      replaced with an enclosing-function one.
//
// This file carries a .go.txt extension deliberately: it is parsed from
// source bytes by go/parser, never built by `go build`/gofmt/go vet/the
// linter, so it is not swept by any of them.
package badpkg

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/qdrant/go-client/qdrant"
	"github.com/seanb4t/engram/internal/store"
)

func TestBadPkgBypassesSeam(t *testing.T) {
	var c *qdrant.Client
	s := store.New(c, "hardcoded-bad-pkg-collection")
	_ = s
}

// TestBadPkgBypassesSeamViaVariable is the variable-indirection bypass.
// The collection argument is an *ast.Ident rather than an *ast.BasicLit,
// so a rule keyed on the argument's SHAPE cannot see it at all, even
// though it reaches Qdrant with an unprefixed name exactly as the literal
// form above does.
func TestBadPkgBypassesSeamViaVariable(t *testing.T) {
	var c *qdrant.Client
	name := "hardcoded-bad-pkg-collection-via-var"
	s := store.New(c, name)
	_ = s
}
